candidates.exact_span: Industrial Users are Non-Significant Categorical Industrial Users (NSCIUs) or Middle Tier CIUs
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether an industrial user is classified as an NSCIU or Middle Tier CIU determines which tier of pretreatment monitoring and reporting obligations apply; misclassification would change which monitoring requirements are treated as applicable for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Industrial Users subject to categorical Pretreatment Standards that are subject to reduced monitoring and reporting requirements under 40 CFR 403.12(e)(2) & (3)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Eligibility for reduced monitoring and reporting under 40 CFR 403.12(e)(2) and (3) directly affects whether full categorical monitoring was required during FY2025 and how missing or non-numeric results should be interpreted when ordinary compliance monitoring may not have been obligated.

candidates.exact_span: Industrial Users subject to the following categorical Pretreatment Standards [Organic Chemicals, Plastics, and Synthetic Fibers (OCPSF) (40 CFR part 414), Petroleum Refining (40 CFR part 419), and Pesticide Chemicals (40 CFR part 455)] and for which the Control Authority has chosen to use the concentration-based standards rather than converting them to flow-based mass standards as allowed at 40 CFR 403.6(c)(6)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The control authority's choice to retain concentration-based standards instead of converting to flow-based mass standards under 40 CFR 403.6(c)(6) changes the form and value of the enforceable numeric limit used for compliance comparison and the monitoring basis tied to those limits.

candidates.exact_span: Categorical Industrial Users subject to concentration-based standards for which the Control Authority has chosen to convert the concentration-based standards to equivalent mass limits, as allowed at 40 CFR 403.6(c)(5)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conversion of concentration-based categorical standards to equivalent mass limits under 40 CFR 403.6(c)(5) changes the applicable enforceable numeric limit and whether reported measurements must be compared on a mass basis rather than a concentration basis.

candidates.exact_span: General Control Mechanisms used for similar groups of SIUs along with the substantially similar types of operations and the types of wastes that are the same, for each separate General Control Mechanism, as allowed at 40 CFR 403.8(f)(1)(iii)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assignment of industrial users to a General Control Mechanism under 40 CFR 403.8(f)(1)(iii) can determine whether shared limits and monitoring requirements apply to a facility rather than individual categorical limits, changing applicable numeric limits and monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: Best Management Practices or Pollution Prevention alternatives required by a categorical Pretreatment Standard or as a local limit requirement that are
candidates.computation_change_reason: Where BMP or pollution-prevention alternatives substitute for or supplement numeric pretreatment standards, interpretation of their applicability affects whether enforceable numeric limits apply, whether conventional monitoring was required, and how absence of ordinary numeric reported results should be classified.
